title: II–III. Names and attributes distinguished; what divine names are
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): II. In ye essence belonging toward GOD ye divine names plus attributes are to be considered. Many ancients plus moderns ye names plus attributes belonging toward God for ye same take, so that ye essential attributes or properties belonging toward God also names they call. But since ye propriety belonging toward words we ought to study, here ye names belonging toward God from ye essential attributes or properties to distinguish we preferred. III. Divine names are those by which God in ye sacred letters is called, that by them, as far as us concerns, His nature may be explained. Ye name belonging toward God in ye Scriptures various things signifies. First, a mark by which God is designated plus from creatures discerned (Genesis 32:29; Exodus 3:15 plus 14:5). Second, God Himself (Deuteronomy 28; Psalm 5:12 plus 7:18 plus 20:2 plus 116:4; Proverbs 18:10). Third, ye power plus grace belonging toward God (Psalm 118:10-12). Fourth, ye will plus commandment belonging toward God (Deuteronomy 18:19; 1 Samuel 17:45; John 5:43; Luke 24:47). Fifth, ye worship, invocation, celebration, profession belonging toward God plus faith (Micah 4:5; Matthew 28:19; Acts 21:13). Here in ye first signification we take it.
pass_b_english: II. In the essence of GOD the divine names and attributes are to be considered. Many ancients and moderns take the names and attributes of God for the same, so that they also call the essential attributes or properties of God names. But since we ought to study the propriety of words, we preferred here to distinguish the names of God from the essential attributes or properties.

III. Divine names are those by which God is called in the sacred letters, that by them, as far as concerns us, His nature may be explained. The name of God in the Scriptures signifies various things. First, a mark by which God is designated and discerned from creatures (Genesis 32:29; Exodus 3:15 and 14:5). Second, God Himself (Deuteronomy 28; Psalm 5:12 and 7:18 and 20:2 and 116:4; Proverbs 18:10). Third, the power and grace of God (Psalm 118:10-12). Fourth, the will and commandment of God (Deuteronomy 18:19; 1 Samuel 17:45; John 5:43; Luke 24:47). Fifth, the worship, invocation, celebration, profession of God and faith (Micah 4:5; Matthew 28:19; Acts 21:13). We take it here in the first signification.
source_text: II. In essentia DEI consideranda sunt nomina & attributa divina. Multi veteres & juniores nomina & attributa Dei pro iisdem capiunt, ita ut attributa sive proprietates Dei essentiales etiam appellent nomina. At, cum nos proprietati vocum studere debeamus, nomina Dei ab attributis sive proprietatibus essentialibus hic distinguere maluimus. III. Nomina divina sunt, quibus Deus in sacris literis appellatur, ut iis, quantum nostra refert, natura illius explicetur. Nomen Dei in scripturis varia significat. Primo, notam, qua Deus designatur & a creaturis discernitur, Gen. 32.29; Exod. 3.15 & 14.5. Secundo, Deum ipsum, Deut. 28; Psal. 5.12 & 7.18 & 20.2 & 116.4; Prov. 18.10. Tertio, potentiam & gratiam Dei, Psal. 118.10.11.12. Quarto, voluntatem & mandatum Dei, Deut. 18.19; 1 Sam. 17.45; Joh. 5.43; Luc. 24.47. Quinto, cultum, invocationem, celebrationem, professionem Dei ac fidem, Mich. 4.5; Matth. 28.19; Act. 21.13. Nos in prima significatione hic accipimus.
